cards.title: The counter is a safety checkpoint
cards.body: Behind the small talk, a good chemist is quietly checking several things before handing over your strip.

cards.title: Is this the right medicine?
cards.body: Many medicine names look and sound alike, especially in handwriting. Chemists check the name makes sense for the patient.

cards.title: Is the strength right?
cards.body: Same medicine, different strength. The chemist checks the number matches the prescription.

cards.title: Does the dose make sense?
cards.body: An unusual dose or frequency gets a second look, and sometimes a call to the doctor.

cards.title: Any clash with other medicines?
cards.body: If they know what else you take, they can spot combinations worth checking.

cards.title: Is it for the right person?
cards.body: Children and older adults may need different doses. That's why the chemist asks who it's for.

cards.title: Help them help you
cards.body: A clear prescription, the full medicine list, and patience while they double-check. A pause at the counter is a good sign.

takeaway: Chemists check name, strength, dose, clashes and the patient. Giving them full information makes those checks work.
share: Send this to whoever gets impatient when the chemist re-reads the parchi.
